summary_paragraph: A woman with complex bariatric surgical history (prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with later reversal) complicated by chronic epigastric pain, gastroparesis with chronic nausea/vomiting, and post–gastric bypass hypoglycemia presented with new acute right-sided abdominal pain radiating to the back and poor oral intake. CT abdomen/pelvis showed a malpositioned feeding tube terminating in the anterior abdominal wall without collection, obstruction, or pneumoperitoneum; right upper quadrant ultrasound and liver/pancreatic labs were unremarkable. Surgery removed the malpositioned tube without incident and did not recommend further surgical intervention at this facility. Symptoms persisted with intermittent soft blood pressures and borderline hypoglycemia attributed to poor intake, managed with IV fluids and dextrose-containing fluids, antiemetics, and transition from IV morphine (worsened nausea) to low-dose oral oxycodone with some improvement. Nutrition evaluated for malnutrition risk; vitamin D deficiency was treated with weekly high-dose repletion and iron deficiency was noted with recommendation to consider outpatient IV iron. Given ongoing pain and inability to meet nutritional needs by mouth with high risk of repeat tube placement or IV nutrition, discharge planning focused on transfer to the patient’s primary surgeon’s hospital for further management, with discharge to extended care in the interim.
